questions.stem: At dynamic equilibrium, which statement is correct?

options.text: The forward and reverse reactions have both stopped
The concentrations of reactants and products are equal
The rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction
Only the forward reaction is still occurring

questions.explanation: At dynamic equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction. Both reactions continue to occur (which is why it is called 'dynamic'), but there is no net change in concentrations. The concentrations are constant but not necessarily equal to each other.

questions.stem: Which conditions are necessary for dynamic equilibrium to be established?

options.text: An irreversible reaction in an open container
A reversible reaction in a closed system
A reversible reaction with a catalyst present

questions.explanation: Dynamic equilibrium requires a reversible reaction in a closed system (where no substances can enter or leave). In an open system, products can escape, preventing the reverse reaction from occurring and so equilibrium cannot be reached. A catalyst is not required for equilibrium.
